title: Jack and the Beanstalk – Bedtime Story for Toddlers – Read Aloud with Pictures
hook: A slow, gentle retelling of Jack and the Beanstalk for 18 months to 4 years, read aloud with picture-book pages (17 pages, about 7 seconds each, with a pause after every page), then a calm flower-garden wind-down. A soft music-box Greensleeves plays under the story. Read it together; ask what Jack should do next.
diff: The only prose flagship and the only one built on the story scene: a 17-page narrated picture book with page turns, a title page and a moral, which no other flagship contains (the rhyme episode is short verse on single pages; the learn episode is flashcards). It runs at 72 BPM in learn mode under Greensleeves — a melody and tempo used nowhere else — and closes with a single flower-garden loop under Grieg's Morning Mood rather than a dance or sleep loop. Age band (18 months–4 years), narration length (about 2.5 minutes of continuous reading) and the fairy-tale cast (Jack, his mother, the giant, the hen, the harp) are unique to this episode.
